ideas.title: Portfolio selection of the top 3 by posterior expected-maximum with mechanism-cluster correlation
ideas.sketch: Replace 'take the 3 highest Bradley-Terry / Plackett-Luce scores' in the final selection step with a set-selection rule. Draw K=2000 posterior samples of the score vector (bootstrap over the pairwise comparisons, refit BT each time). Have one cheap role-agent label each finalist with a mechanism cluster (which core lever the idea pulls, not its topic). Add a shared cluster-level random shift to the sampled scores so that ideas in one cluster are positively correlated, as they will be in practice. Then greedily pick the 3-set that maximises the mean over samples of the best idea in the set, with a tie-break towards more distinct clusters. This corrects a real failure of top-3-by-score: near-duplicate winners that succeed or fail together, which wastes the slots. A single agent that self-selects 3 from its own 20 tends to pick 3 variants of its favourite theme and has no posterior to hedge with. Test it on/off in the scoring module only, with everything upstream identical. Measures: best-of-3 and mean rated score against the blinded panel, and the number of distinct clusters in the delivered top 3. The gain concentrates on briefs where raters disagree or where outcomes are heavy-tailed, and the change adds no judge tokens beyond one labelling call.

ideas.title: Loss-conditioned revision with a monotone acceptance test and a fixed card budget
ideas.sketch: Add a revision loop after the first pairwise round. Each finalist's developer receives the judges' written reasons from the comparisons it lost, and must fix only the specific weakness those reasons cite. Hard constraint: the revised card has the same token budget as the original, so a revision cannot win by growing longer or more polished. The revision is then tested against its own original in a position-swapped pair judged by a different model family from the generator and the developer. It is accepted only if it wins both orderings, otherwise the original stays. Accepted revisions re-enter the Plackett-Luce fit as replacement items. This is hill-climbing with a verifier. It gives the pipeline something a single agent lacks, which is an independent adversary's stated reasons for why an idea lost, and it protects against the usual failure of self-revision, where 'improvements' are cosmetic or dilute the idea. Test it on/off at the development phase: the fraction of revisions accepted, and the blinded panel's ratings of final cards revised versus unrevised. A word-count-matched control and a family-swapped rater panel check that the gain is not from length or style.
